svg.title: Galen's Animal-Derived Anatomy (2nd Century AD — Pig, Ape & Dog Dissection)
svg.desc: Edexcel GCSE History anatomical comparison diagram illustrating Claudius Galen's major anatomical errors derived from dissecting Barbary apes, pigs, and dogs: a two-bone mandible, a seven-segment sternum, invisible pores across the cardiac septum, a five-lobed liver clasping the stomach, and a rete mirabile vascular net at the base of the brain.
svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · CLASSICAL MEDICAL DOGMA (BEFORE VESALIUS)
Galen's Animal-Derived Anatomy (2nd Century AD — Pig, Ape & Dog Dissection)
GALENIC COMPOSITE MODEL (ANIMAL PROXIES APPLIED TO HUMANS)

svg.text: DISSECTION SOURCE: PIGS, BARBARY APES & DOGS

g.text: ERROR 1 · MANDIBLE
Two-Bone Animal Jawbone
Galen taught the lower human jaw is made of two separate
bones joined at the chin — copied directly from dissecting
dogs and Barbary macaque apes rather than human skulls.
WHY GALEN MADE THESE ERRORS
Roman Taboo Against Human Dissection
Roman law & religion forbade cutting open human corpses.
Except for wounded gladiators in Pergamum, Galen relied
almost entirely on pigs (organs) and apes (muscles/bones).
ERROR 3 · HEART WALL
Invisible "Pores" in the Cardiac Septum
Claimed tiny invisible pores perforated the central septum
wall so venous blood could seep from the right ventricle
into the left ventricle to mix with inhaled pneuma.
CONTINUITY · c.1250–1500
1,400 Years of Unquestioned Authority
• Church Endorsement: Galen wrote that the body's design
proved one Creator, fitting Christian theology.
• Book-Led Training: Rare medieval dissections were read
aloud from Galen merely to prove him right, never to test
him — anomalies were blamed on an "imperfect corpse".
• Over 300 anatomical errors went uncorrected until 1543.
CRANIAL ERROR · BASE OF BRAIN
Supposed Rete Mirabile ("Wonderful Net")
Galen described a dense tangled mesh of blood vessels —
the rete mirabile — beneath the human brain, claiming it
refined vital spirits into animal spirits for the nerves.
• Actually exists in ungulates (pigs, sheep & oxen) to cool
brain blood while grazing — absent in humans.
ERROR 2 · BREASTBONE
Seven-Segment Ape Sternum
Asserted the human breastbone consists of seven separate
bone segments stacked in a chain — accurate for apes
and monkeys, but false for adult human anatomy.
SCHOLASTIC TRANSMISSION
Hand-Copied Manuscripts & Dogma
Monastic scribes copied Galen's texts without accurate
life drawings; questioning Galen risked charges of heresy.
ERROR 4 · HEPATIC ANATOMY
Five-Lobed Animal Liver Clasping Stomach
Described a five-lobed liver spreading finger-like lobes
around the stomach — copied from dissecting pigs & dogs.
• Combined with the false rete mirabile, these errors
distorted Western understanding of digestion, blood
production, and internal surgery for 14 centuries.

svg.text: EDEXCEL EXAM TAKEAWAY · WHY GALEN'S ANATOMY BLOCKED PROGRESS UNTIL THE RENAISSANCE
Because Galen dissected animals rather than humans — and the Medieval Church protected his writings as sacred authority — physicians
repeated animal anatomy errors for 1,400 years instead of observing real human bodies directly.
